Clarification required

PLAN — Issue: activation gap from PR #6643 (the live merged-PR guard hook still reads the TTL cache on pushes)

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `2774a92644e6971ded69b5b39788dde17efac4f9`, branch `main`. The issue has no integration-branch metadata, so there is no mismatch.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py
Scope-mode justification: The template copy of the hook already contains the #6641 fix: a push never reads the TTL cache, and a cache-derived snapshot is re-queried once. Only the live copy `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` is behind. Copying the template over the live file byte for byte is the whole fix and the smallest change. It also makes the two parity tests that currently fail on `main` pass. No logic is written by hand, and no tests, docs or other files need to change. Expansion is not warranted, because writing `files_touched` into activation-fix issues is a separate defect (see Risks). Reduction is not possible.

## Verified evidence (read on this ref)
- `diff .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` shows exactly the #6641 hunks:
  - **Shared PR-lookup memo:** in the live copy, a push can be decided from the TTL cache or from a cache-derived snapshot memoized by an earlier `git commit`; the template does not allow either.
  - **Push check:** the live copy reads `_read_cache`, issues a live query only on a cached block, and writes the cache only when it was cold. The template always calls `query_pull_requests` and then `_write_cache`.
  - **Docstrings and comments:** the template adds the §21.D notes.
- Both files have mode `-rwxr-xr-x`, so the parity test also compares executable bits and the copy must keep the mode.
- `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py` loads the live copy (`GUARD_PATH`). `test_template_copies_are_identical` (around line 2301) asserts byte equality and fails today. `tests/test_claude_template_live_parity.py::test_live_copies_match_their_templates` also fails.
- `.github/ai/claude_template_divergence.json` does not list this hook, so it must not diverge.
- The live-copy cache tests stay valid after the copy:
  - `_evaluate()` runs `git commit -m x`, and a commit may still use the cache, so `test_block_is_reverified_live_before_firing` and `test_cached_allow_issues_no_api_call` still pass.
  - `test_cached_merged_pr_is_rechecked_once_for_repeated_targets` (push) still expects exactly one live call, which the template behaviour gives.
- The #6641 test block (around line 3029) already tests the template copy (`fresh_state_guard`).
- `changelog.d/6641-merge-guard-push-fresh-pr-state.md` already describes this behaviour and has not been assembled yet.

## 1. Files likely to change
- `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`: overwrite with the exact bytes of `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` and keep mode 0755.

Nothing else changes:
- Not the template.
- Not the tests: they already encode the target behaviour.
- Not the divergence allowlist.
- No changelog fragment: the 6641 fragment covers it, and a second one would duplicate the entry.
- Not `.ai/.workspace_source_manifest.txt`: it is gitignored here.

## 2. Functions or modules to implement
None are written by hand. Copying the file brings in the template versions of the shared PR-lookup memo, the push check and their docstrings.

## 3. Data structures affected
None on disk. In memory, the memoized PR snapshot is re-queried once for a push when it came from the cache (template semantics). The TTL cache file format does not change.

## 4. API or interface changes
- No CLI, environment, log-key or exit-code changes.
- Behaviour change for interactive sessions in this repo: `git push` and GitHub MCP pushes always do one live PR lookup per branch per guarded command. When that lookup fails, the guard follows §21.C: it blocks when git history shows stranded work and otherwise asks for confirmation. A bare `git commit` may still be allowed from the cache.

## Decisions
### D1 — Byte copy of the template instead of re-applying the hunks
- Chosen: copy the whole file from the template (for example `cp` or `install -m 0755`) and confirm with `cmp`.
- Alternatives considered: re-applying the diff hunks by hand; listing the hook in `claude_template_divergence.json`.
- Why: the parity tests require identical bytes and executable bits. Copying by hand risks small differences. Allowlisting a security hook would hide exactly the drift the activation check found.

### D2 — No new changelog fragment
- Chosen: rely on the existing `changelog.d/6641-merge-guard-push-fresh-pr-state.md`.
- Alternatives considered: adding a `changelog.d/<issue>-live-merge-guard-sync.md` fragment.
- Why: the user-visible change is already described and has not been released yet, so a second entry would duplicate it (CLAUDE.md §20, one entry per change).

## Security considerations
- Trust boundary: this is the interactive merged-PR guard (CLAUDE.md §21.C/§21.D). Bringing the live copy up to date removes a way around it. A cached "open PR" result, which can be up to 300 seconds stale or planted as a file in the temp directory, could allow a push to a branch whose PR has already merged.
- Authorization: no new surface. The change narrows what the guard trusts: a push trusts only live GitHub state.
- External input: unchanged. The PR-state JSON from `gh` is parsed as before.
- Abuse cases closed:
  - A forged or stale cache entry allowing a push to a merged branch.
  - A `git commit && git push` in one command reusing a cache-derived snapshot for the push.
- No secrets are involved.

## 5. Risks and edge cases
- **Implement guard (blocker):** `.claude/` is an automation path. `scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py::build_automation_grant` grants an automation path only from an exact `files_touched:` block in the issue body. This issue has no such block, so the implement commit will be rejected with `IMPLEMENT_AUTOMATION_PATH_GUARD ... reason=no_allowlist` and `ai:scope-blocked`. The unblock judge cannot override this rejection. agents.md also notes that pipeline editors generally cannot fix `.claude/**` live copies.
- **Held sync PR (unverified):** #6643 merged from an `ai/*` head, so `sync-claude-live-copies.yml` most likely put this path in the held draft branch `ai/sync-claude-live-copies-held` rather than the auto-mergeable branch. I could not confirm this: `gh` is not available in the planning sandbox. If that held PR is reviewed and merged first, this issue's implementation becomes a no-op.
- **Upstream defect, out of scope:** `scripts/activation_verify.sh` files code-gap issues for automation paths without a `files_touched:` block. Any such issue will hit the same guard. A follow-up issue should track this.
- Consumer repos are unaffected: they already receive the hook from the template on `@stable` sync.

## 6. Testing considerations
- `cmp .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` returns 0, and `stat -c %a` shows 755 on both.
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -m pytest tests/test_claude_template_live_parity.py tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py -q` should pass, in particular:
  - `test_template_copies_are_identical`
  - `test_live_copies_match_their_templates`
  - the `_evaluate` commit-path cache tests
  - `test_cached_merged_pr_is_rechecked_once_for_repeated_targets`
- `python -m py_compile .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`
- In CI, the `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` job's sync dry-run never prepares `.claude/hooks/**`, so the committed live copy must match the template. This change provides that.

## Automation (§20.E)
- **Scripts:** none added; this only modifies an existing file.
- **Scheduler entry point:** none. The copy is consumed by interactive sessions, and parity is enforced by `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and the release gates' `validate-scripts` parity step.
- **Supervisor:** none.
- **DB work:** none.
- **Removal registry (`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`):** no entry needed.

## Clarification required before implementation

> **Q1: The implement guard will reject any commit touching `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`, because this issue's body has no `files_touched:` grant. How should the live copy land?**
>
> Choices:
> - **A** — A trusted maintainer (or the pipeline's own account) edits this issue's body to add a `files_touched:` block listing exactly `- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`, then re-runs `/approved`. The plan above then applies unchanged. (RECOMMENDED)
> - **B** — A human reviews and merges the held sync PR from `ai/sync-claude-live-copies-held`, or does the byte copy in an interactive session, then closes this issue as satisfied. No pipeline implementation is needed.
> - **C** — Run implementation without the grant. The commit will be rejected with `ai:scope-blocked` (`guard=automation-path`, which cannot be overridden).
>
> Reply: `Q1: A`

Note: an automatic `Q1: A` answer does not edit the issue body by itself. Option A still needs the body edit to happen before implementation.

PLAN_SELF_CHECK: BLOCKER: implement's automation-path guard requires an exact `files_touched:` grant for `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` in the issue body, and this issue (from the activation verifier) has none, so the commit would be rejected as `ai:scope-blocked` with no override.

Actions taken: read the hook diff, the parity and hook tests, the divergence allowlist, the sync script constants, the automation-path grant logic in `scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py` and the implement wiring for it; no repository files were changed.
Assumptions: the #6643 sync was most likely held because its head branch was `ai/*`; I could not confirm this because `gh` is not available here.
